paragraphs: Rav Ilish, end of Tamid Nishḥat. According to the account Heilprin goes on to dispute, he knew the language of birds and went to try to rescue Rav Naḥman’s daughters; see his entry, Gittin, HaShole'aḥ. Arukh, Mal 8, says Rav Ilish knew birds' speech: a dove chirped 'Ilish, flee,' and he escaped. End of quotation. See, my brother, this is not so. Gittin 45a says Rav Ilish was captured; a man who knew birds' speech sat beside him. A raven called; Ilish asked the man what it said—Rashi specifies the speakers. He answered, 'Ilish, flee; Ilish, flee.' Ilish called the raven a liar and would not rely on it. A dove came; he again asked, receiving the same answer. Israel's congregation is compared to a dove, so he inferred a miracle. He and the man fled—Rashi: Rav Ilish and the bird-language interpreter. Ilish crossed by ferry through a miracle; the other was found and killed. End of Gemara. Clearly Rav Ilish did not know the language, but the other man did. How could Arukh and Yuḥasin write the opposite? Musaf HeArukh also missed the correction. Rava calls Rav Ilish a great man, Bava Metzia 68b. Rav Ilish intended to speak before Rava; he answered concerning judges of Ḥatzatzta, etc.; Ilish was ashamed, and Rava said, 'I am the Lord; in its time I shall hasten it,' Bava Batra 133b. Rav Ilish spoke to Rava, who was ashamed, Gittin 77b; Rav Ilish also spoke to Rava, Bava Metzia 96a. Rav Ilish was the mystical rectification of Bela, king of Sodom; see Rav Naḥman.
